alignment.rule: Baseline result rows 0-52 map directly to source scenarios 0-52. Baseline result rows 53-105 map to source scenarios 54-106. Source scenario 53 is retained as an incorrect no-diagnosis result.

rubric.correct: The response definitively asserts the reference disease, an accepted synonym, or a compatible subtype. A correct underlying diagnosis remains correct when a complication or secondary diagnosis is also stated.
rubric.incorrect: The response gives a different disease, only a cause or manifestation of the reference disease, an overly broad category that does not identify the reference disease, or an unresolved differential containing alternatives.
rubric.borderline: A semantically related answer for which acceptance depends on whether the evaluator permits a parent category, missing acute/chronic or in-situ specificity, or an unresolved alternative.

baseline.reason: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is an insufficiently specific parent category for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
Post-micturition syncope is a subtype of situational syncope and exactly matches the described trigger.
Benign cystic lesion does not identify an epidermoid cyst.
Post-viral exanthem is too generic and does not identify erythema infectiosum.
Active hepatitis B infection omits the clinically important chronic classification required by the reference.
Labyrinthitis or vestibular neuritis is an unresolved differential between distinct diseases.
Schizophrenia is not equivalent to schizophreniform disorder; duration is diagnostically defining.

pnlc.reason: Vasovagal syncope does not identify the reference post-micturition situational syncope.
Mallet finger is an extensor injury, whereas the reference is flexor digitorum profundus avulsion at its insertion.
The response explicitly diagnoses osteoarthritis; the unsupported gout addition is answer contamination but does not erase the correct primary diagnosis.
The response explicitly identifies congestive heart failure as secondary to the reference atrial septal defect.
The response explicitly diagnoses oppositional defiant disorder; the additional reading disorder does not erase the correct primary diagnosis.
